task: Add review 4's W1 cases (R16, DEC-987) to W2-96's acceptance suite, show them red on the head, then make one try at removing the empty leftover folder in the W2-96 worktree.
status: DONE — both R16 cases are committed and red on the head in 4 runs of 4. The other 106 cases still pass. The leftover folder could not be removed: the sandbox refused the `rmdir` (read-only file system), and I took that refusal.
work_completed: New file `test_w2_96_at_review_4.py` with two cases and one premise, written in the harness's form. The outer planted test runs `python3 -m gov.cli.main accept` on a nested planted project, in a session of its own. The nested run's `TMPDIR` is `<outer tmp_path>/qzv96leak-given-1`, and its environment carries a token for the case (`QZV96LEAK_R16_RUN=qzv96leak-r16-<uuid>`). The nested test records when it starts sleeping, sleeps 5 s, then passes. The case finds the run's processes by that token (in `/proc/<pid>/environ` or `cmdline`) and by the process ids the planted tests recorded, never by a name. (1) The stopped run: SIGTERM goes to the outer gov alone once the nested test is sleeping, and the case checks the nested pytest was still running when it went. Expected: exit 143; the given `TMPDIR` empty and no marker when gov ends; no process of the run alive at that moment; the given `TMPDIR` still empty later. (2) The run that does not wait: the planted test returns, passing, once the nested test sleeps; no signal. Expected: both lines pass, exit 0, and the same process and later checks. Each case runs 2 races and fails at the first bad one, and each case's own clean-up kills every process carrying the token or recorded. The support module gained only additions; no earlier case changed. The README gained the two map rows (with their expected red reasons), the review 4 premise in the premises row, a "Review 4's cases" section and two "Choices" bullets.

- **Sandbox check:** (a) the write failed with `OSError: [Errno 30] Read-only file system`, and no file was made. (b) `git hash-object -w` returned `1ae28402a109…` and `git update-index --refresh` gave rc 0. `GOV_ROLE=independent-test-designer`, `GOV_TICKET=DAEO-ouet`; the top level is `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-96-tests` on `w2/W2-96-tests`. `.git/hooks` holds only `*.sample` files, so no `pre-commit`.
- **Commit:** `4b9353954f88` "W2-96 (DAEO-ouet): review 4's W1 cases for gov accept, no process of the run outlives it (DEC-987)", trailers `Task: DAEO-ouet`, `Role: independent-test-designer`, `Implements: DEC-987, DEC-959`, `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. `git log --oneline -2` shows `4b935395` on top of `943543ce`.

- **Red reasons as seen (both cases, every run):**
  - "2 processes of the run still run once gov accept ended": the nested `python3 -m gov.cli.main accept TDPL-a961 --json` and its `python3 -B -m pytest …`.
  - "the given TMPDIR holds 6 entries 8.4–9.0 s after gov accept ended (it held none when gov ended)": `gov-accept-XXXX/tmp/pytest-of-usain/pytest-0/test_qzv96leak_r16_…0/qzv96leak-given-1`, the same 6 entries review 4 reported.
  - "a name left in the given TMPDIR after gov ended holds the marker".
  - The stopped run exited 143 and the other exited 0 with the expected result; both had the given `TMPDIR` empty when gov ended. So the red comes from R16 alone.
- **Orphan check after the runs:** no process carried the token, and no `accept TDPL-a961` process was found.
- **`gov retrieve`:** not used. The suite, the ticket's KPIs and DEC-987 were enough, so no result under `src/gov/accept/` or `tests/unit/accept/` was served. I read no implementation file.
- **Leftover folder:** `ls -la` showed it empty (only `.` and `..`). `rmdir /home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-96/tests/acceptance/.claude/.cc-writes` was refused word for word: `rmdir: failed to remove '/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-96/tests/acceptance/.claude/.cc-writes': Read-only file system`. Because that failed I did not try the parent, and used no other form.
- **Guard read refusals met:** 0.
- **Scratch measure:** `du -sh` gives 6.1M and `du -s --inodes` gives 1553 for `/tmp/gov-os-lead-W2-96/gov-launch-independent-test-designer-r6gslyyk`. Most of it is pytest's kept temp folders of the failed cases (retention `failed`).
tests:
- New file alone, run 1: 2 failed, 1 passed (20.7 s).
- Whole W2-96 folder (`--tb=line`): 2 failed, 107 passed, in 135 s. The 107 are the 106 earlier cases plus the new premise.
- New file, run 2: 2 failed, 1 passed (19.8 s).
- New file, run 3: 2 failed, 1 passed (19.4 s).
- `test_w2_96_at_premises.py` after the last README edit: 10 passed.
- Both cases were red at race 1 in every run. Load average was 18 to 25 throughout.
discoveries:
- On the head the red is deterministic, not a race: the nested gov and its pytest are always still alive when the outer gov ends, so the process check fails before the later look at the `TMPDIR`. The 6 leftover entries also appeared in every run.
- The `qzv96leak-given-1` name is the last of the 6 entries, so the leftover names carry the marker.
risks:
- I could not check the cases against a correct implementation; I reasoned it through only. The case requires every process gone at gov's end with no grace, as R16 says. An implementation that kills the processes but leaves the reaping to init could fail it.
- A green race costs about 12 s, so the suite adds roughly 50 s when green (my estimate). The folder took 135 s when red, so it should stay well under eight minutes.
- The nested pytest is found by the token only if gov passes its environment on; the case finds it by its recorded pid in any case.
lessons:
- In this sandbox each Bash call has its own process namespace (low pids such as 16 and 17), so a check for orphans from a later command sees nothing of an earlier one. The cases' own clean-up is what guarantees no orphans.
- The worktree top shows sandbox placeholder dotfiles as untracked files. Never `git add -A` there.
proposed_decisions: none
unresolved: The empty folders `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-96/tests/acceptance/.claude/.cc-writes` and its parent `.claude/` are still there. This role's sandbox cannot write in the W2-96 worktree, so a session that can write there (the lead's) has to remove them.
recommended_next_action: The lead merges `w2/W2-96-tests` (`4b9353954f88`) into `w2/W2-96`, removes the two empty folders from the W2-96 worktree with its own write access, and starts the engineer on R16 (a subreaper that reaps every process before the clean-up).
